text:
Matvei Michkov's week was the Flyers' biggest story. He was a healthy scratch for Friday's game against Vancouver, which the team called an internal matter (PHLY Sports reported Rick Tocchet gave no details), and the home crowd answered with a "We want Michkov" chant. Tocchet said afterward he'd be back in the lineup Saturday, and that Michkov had been in the locker room "high-fiving guys after the win." Around the same time, reports said Daniel Brière had turned away teams calling about a trade.

The hockey has its own tension. Michkov has 11 goals in 27 games, but on just 6.4 expected goals, shooting 28.9% against a normal of about 14.6% by our numbers. That won't last. At the same time, Philadelphia has scored 10.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that gap should close. The bigger worry is the five-on-five share: the Flyers get just 42% of the expected goals with him out there.

His minutes tell the rest: 12:18 in Washington, his lowest of the season. He's 21, a seventh overall pick producing well above the 0.40 median for his draft slot. Watch his ice time.
